subject: Interim notice — Helios-2m elevated 5xx/timeouts and immediate mitigations
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elena@vertexanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interim notice — Helios-2m elevated 5xx/timeouts and immediate mitigations

Hi Elena,

We wanted to let you know we are currently observing an elevated rate of 5xx errors and request timeouts for requests routed to model "Helios-2m" in the us-west region. Symptoms started around 08:55 PT this morning and are most visible on generation requests with context windows >~2k tokens and on streaming sessions.

What we know so far:
- Impact: increased 5xx responses and occasional client-side streaming timeouts; affects ~3% of Vertex Analytics production requests (our routing logs).
- Root area under investigation: an interaction between recent kernel scheduling changes and the Helios KV-cache for long contexts.
- Immediate mitigations applied: traffic reroute to Helios-2m-fallback and tightened request timeouts for heavy-context requests.

Attachments: helio_error_log_snippet.txt (excerpted errors, timestamps), mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf (short checklist).

Next steps from our side:
1) Ops has a hotfix rolling to the Helios serving nodes (ETA 2–3 hours).
2) We'll keep your traffic on the fallback variant for the next 24 hours while we validate stability.
3) Postmortem with timeline and impact analysis will be shared within 72 hours.

Immediate asks for Vertex Analytics:
- If you have any short-lived heavy-context jobs that can be delayed ~3–4 hours, please pause them to reduce load while we finish the patch validation.
- Share any request_ids (if available) from observed errors — that speeds triage.

I will post updates in this thread. Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your production SLA and we’re prioritizing stabilization and a follow-up with remediation and credit options.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Helios-2m incident update and next steps (post-stabilization)

Hi Elena — follow-up and short post-incident summary now that the Helios-2m rollout is stable: 

Summary and timeline (high level):
- 2029-06-18 08:55 PT — anomaly detection flagged elevated 5xx rates vs baseline for Helios-2m.
- 2029-06-18 09:00–10:30 PT — emergency routing: traffic shifted to Helios-2m-fallback; retries/timeouts tightened for long-context requests.
- 2029-06-18 10:15 PT — ops validated fallback performance; hotfix for kernel scheduler queued.
- 2029-06-18 12:10 PT — hotfix deployed to a canary subset (no regression observed).
- 2029-06-18 14:30 PT — full rollout completed; error rates returned to baseline by ~15:05 PT.

Root cause (brief):
- A kernel scheduling change reduced the effectiveness of our KV-cache eviction policy under long-context workloads, which increased memory churn and led to intermittent request failures on affected Helios nodes.

Actions taken:
- Deployed scheduler hotfix reverting the offending optimization and restoring the original eviction thresholds.
- Added tighter health probes to detect early KV-cache regressions and automated rollbacks for canaries.
- Updated routing policy to avoid Helios-2m for requests with context >2k until we ship a long-term cache improvement (target Q4 2029).

Impact and mitigation for Vertex Analytics:
- We estimate Vertex saw a ~3.1% uplift in 5xx/timeout responses during the 5-hour window; user-facing sessions impacted for ~22 minutes of peak disruption. (We’ll share sanitized request-level logs separately.)
- Your traffic remained on fallback during the outage; fallback preserves output quality parity >95% of the time for standard prompts, but you may see subtle distribution shifts on very long-form generations. If you’d prefer a stricter quality baseline, we can pin you to a specific controlled variant — Ben can scope that commercially.

Follow-ups and artifacts:
- Full postmortem (timeline, telemetry charts, RCA) is here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3C4D5E6F7G8H9/view?usp=sharing
- HubSpot case: HUBSPOT-CR-48291 (Ben will track credit/reconciliation).
- Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf (updated), helio_error_log_snippet.txt (sanitized).

Next steps for us:
- We’ll run a controlled load test against the long-context path and share results by 2029-07-02.
- Engineering will provide a scheduled roadmap item for a persistent KV-cache improvement (ETA Q4 2029).

If you’d like a synchronous postmortem walk-through with our engineering and product leads, we can set up a 30–45 minute call this week — Ben, can you propose 2 slots?

Apologies again for the interruption; we appreciate your patience and the request ids you shared — those helped speed debugging.

Best regards,
Priyom Das
